title: A piece lines up inside the group that holds it
goal: Lining one thing up works when it sits on a screen, because a screen has a size of its own. It does nothing for a word inside a button, which is the case people hit most while building UI: pick the word, and there is no way to say centre it in the button. Give a piece inside any group the same one-press alignment it gets on a screen.
notes: Follow-up from one-layer-lines-up-inside-the-frame-it-sits-in (2026-09-03), which deliberately stopped at frames. Today EditorState.arrangeReference takes the immediate parent and only when it isFrame, so a piece inside a group gets no row. The hard part is not the maths (LayerArrangement.aligned already takes a container box) but the group-of-one case: a group box is the union of its children, so with one child the reference IS the child and all six buttons are no-ops. Options: hide the row when the parent box equals the layer box on both axes; or dim per axis. Also decide whether aligning a child that currently defines the group edge should be allowed to shrink the group box, which it would today since the box is derived. See docs/design/ui-building.md, One layer lines up inside its screen.
acceptance: With one piece inside a group selected, the Arrange row is there and says it is lining up inside that group
Pressing Align Center puts the piece in the middle of the group, and one undo puts it back
A group whose box is exactly the piece itself offers nothing that does nothing, so no dead buttons
Lining a piece up never changes the size of the group around it
